question: to the Commission Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The Republic of Cyprus, as an island Member State, faces specific challenges in managing foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). The Commission confirmed that preventive vaccination cannot be used in disease-free Member States, while emergency vaccination may be applied in affected areas and that Cyprus had notified three FMD outbreaks in Larnaca on 21 February 2026 and received vaccine doses, support from the European Union Veterinary Emergency Team (EUVET) and emergency assistance. In the areas of Cyprus not under the government’s effective control, where the acquis are suspended under Protocol No 10, the EU continues to support animal-health measures, including veterinary assistance and the delivery of 500 000 FMD vaccine doses in February 2026. 1.

Will the Commission urgently request an assessment by the European Food Safety Authority, with input from EUVET and the EU Reference Laboratory for FMD, on the effectiveness and proportionality of emergency vaccination compared with wider culling under Cyprus’s island conditions, and under what timeframe?

Does the Commission intend to examine whether the EU framework on emergency FMD vaccination should be adapted for island Member States, including on recovery periods, movement derogations and recovery arrangements?

Will the Commission strengthen the conditions attached to EU animal-health support in areas not under government control by requiring verifiable FMD-control benchmarks, including surveillance, vaccination records, movement controls, traceability, outbreak reporting and external audit?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) The EU legal framework, in particular Regulation (EU) 2016/4291 and Commission Delegated Regulations (EU) 2020/6872, 2020/6893 and 2023/3614 provide the instruments to control and eradicate category A diseases such as foot and mouth disease (FMD). Within this framework, the Commission adopted emergency regionalisation measures5. The Commission has supported Cyprus following its FMD outbreaks via several EUVET deployments6 and 1 029 000 vaccine doses from the EU FMD antigen bank7. The EU Reference Laboratory for FMD, which operates under the Official Controls Regulation8, regularly reviews the testing capacities of national reference laboratories, including Cyprus. The Commission has already requested the European Food Safety Authority to assess control measures for Category A diseases in the framework of the Animal Health Law9, including FMD10. The current framework allows flexibility for emergency vaccination based on risk assessments and foresees a timeframe for lifting the measures and movement derogations. The Commission continues to monitor emergency vaccination implementation in Cyprus and assess whether additional action is needed. In the Turkish Cypriot community, the EU Aid Programme11 finances priority animal-health measures. The Commission applies conditionalities adapted to the island-specific circumstances and the financial support available. It promotes a coordinated and effective disease prevention and response, including by supporting the work of the bicommunal Veterinary Sub-Committee under the Technical Committee for Health. Such response requires both communities to engage. The delegated body Bureau Veritas (Decision 2021/58612) is bound to deliver reliable and independent information on FMD control activities.
